mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in GDPC1 (nominal personal consumption expenditures) signals robust economic growth, boosting corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC <0.03 over any 3-month window, or 60-day returns in expanding economies are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.0% triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return, signaling aggressive monetary tightening that raises borrowing costs and dampens equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain negative despite FEDFUNDS above 4.0% in the tightening cycle, or Rank IC >0.05 over the period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly UNRATE crossing above 6.0% triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return, reflecting weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not turn negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.0%, or Rank IC >0.05 over the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE below 4.5% signals strengthening labor market conditions, enhancing corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to rise significantly when UNRATE remains below 4.5%, or Rank IC <0.03 over the period.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling FEDFUNDS (easing) and rising GDPC1 (demand) amplifies equity valuation growth, as lower interest rates boost corporate cash flows and stronger demand drives stock prices higher over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns do not outperform baseline when both FEDFUNDS declines and GDPC1 rises, or interaction effect rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in FEDFUNDS (easing) and HOUST (demand) create conflicting signals, yet their combined effect over 20 days drives positive S&P 500 returns as easing lowers discount rates while stronger demand boosts corporate profits.
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to rise when both FEDFUNDS and HOUST move in the predicted directions, or interaction effect rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a sustained FEDFUNDS rise above 3.0% triggers negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as higher interest rates suppress equity valuations and corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.0% in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS above 3.0% in the tightening cycle, or Rank IC >0.05 over the period.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-recession recovery, sustained growth in GDPC1 (demand) alongside falling UNRATE (labor) signals robust economic expansion, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as corporate profits and equity prices rebound.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth exceeds 5% MoM and UNRATE falls below 4.5% in post-recession recovery regime
failure_condition: 60-day returns fail to rise significantly when GDPC1 grows >5% and UNRATE drops <4.5% in the post-recession regime, or Rank IC <0.03 over the period.
